tasks.title: Parsing a dependency string
tasks.statement: Write parse_requirement(text): from a string like "requests>=2.31,<3" return a tuple (name, list of (operator, version) pairs). Ignore spaces around the parts and drop any extras in square brackets. The operators are ==, !=, <=, >=, ~=, <, >. Reject a string that cannot be parsed with ValueError.
tasks.hint: Use the regex ^([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)(?:\[[^\]]*\])?(.*)$ for the name, split the remainder on commas and parse the operator and version.

tasks.title: Comparing versions
tasks.statement: Write compare_versions(a, b): return -1, 0 or 1 for versions like "1.10.2". Compare by numbers, not by strings ("1.10" is newer than "1.2"), and treat missing parts as zeros ("1.0" equals "1.0.0").
tasks.hint: Split on dots into lists of int, pad them with zeros to the same length and compare the lists.

tasks.title: Does a version satisfy a condition
tasks.statement: The function compare_versions is already there. Write satisfies(version, spec): spec is several conditions separated by commas (>=, >, <=, <, ==, !=, ~=). A compatible release ~=1.4.2 means ">=1.4.2 and the version starts with 1.4", and ~=1.4 means ">=1.4 and starts with 1".
tasks.hint: For ~=: the lower bound >= spec, and all parts of the version match except the last part of spec.

tasks.title: Reading pyproject.toml
tasks.statement: Write project_info(text): parse the TOML with the tomllib module and return a tuple (name, version, required Python, list of dependencies) from the [project] section. If a field is missing, use None (for dependencies, an empty list).
tasks.hint: data = tomllib.loads(text).get("project", {}); then data.get("name") and so on.

tasks.title: Entry point
tasks.statement: Write resolve_entry_point(spec): a string like "package.module:function" (as in [project.scripts]) is turned into a callable object; a nested dotted name after the colon is allowed. A format without a colon raises ValueError; a missing module raises ImportError, a missing name raises AttributeError.
tasks.hint: module, sep, attr = spec.partition(":"); if there is no sep, raise ValueError; then import_module and getattr for each part of attr.split(".").

tasks.title: Finding packages in a directory
tasks.statement: Write find_packages(root): a sorted list of the full names of the packages in the directory root, meaning directories with an __init__.py. Descend only into packages (if the parent is not a package, nested ones do not count).
tasks.hint: A recursive function: for each subdirectory with __init__.py, add the name and descend into it with a prefix.

tasks.title: The project's command line
tasks.statement: Write main(argv=None): argparse with a required --name, an optional --times (an integer, 1 by default) and a --shout flag. It prints the greeting "Greetings, <name>!" the required number of times (with --shout, in upper case) and returns 0. An argument error is the normal argparse behavior (SystemExit with code 2).
tasks.hint: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(); parser.add_argument("--name", required=True); --times type=int default=1; --shout action="store_true".

tasks.title: What changed in the lock
tasks.statement: Write lock_diff(old, new): old and new are dicts of package to version. Return a tuple of three sorted lists of strings: added ("+ name version"), removed ("- name version") and updated ("~ name old → new").
tasks.hint: Compare the key sets: new - old, old - new, and the intersection with differing values.

tasks.title: Settings from the environment
tasks.statement: Write load_settings(environ): a dict of settings from environment variables (environ is an ordinary dict): DEBUG ("1", "true", "yes" in any case is True, anything else False), PORT (an integer, 8000 by default; not a number or outside 1..65535 raises ValueError), HOSTS (a list from the comma-separated value with no spaces at the edges, ["localhost"] by default).
tasks.hint: Treat an empty HOSTS as missing; check PORT with int(...) and the range.
